newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan group to visit Okinawa, planning investment.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan group to visit Okinawa, planning investment.

text.p: Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party said on Wednesday it would organize a business mission to Okinawa this month, hoping to nudge Taiwan investors towards Japan's southernmost island -- and away from rival China.
The mission, scheduled to visit Okinawa during from December 14 to 17, would be led by Liu Tai-ying, head of the ruling party's Business Management Committee, officials said.
State-funded television quoted Liu as saying the planned investment in Okinawa would be a maximum of US$1 billion.
A committee spokesman told Reuters the amount of the investment had not yet been decided.
Liu said it would be "good if we can develop Okinawa into a free trade zone", adding that his party was also interested in building shopping malls in Okinawa.
Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui has expressed willingness to visit Japan, where he went to university, but such a visit has not yet been possible because of pressure from China.
Lee is also chairman of the Nationalist Party, one of the world's richest political organisations with T$37.8 billion (US$1.4 billion) in assets under seven holding companies.

Liu has denied speculation that the Okinawa mission was to prepare for Lee's future visit to Japan, saying Okinawa's tourism, electronics processing and aerospace industries were all worthy of investment.
In late October, President Lee expressed his "full support" for the Okinawa trip after being briefed by Liu.
Lee and other party leaders, wary of a risky overdependence on China's economy, have called for diverting investment away from the long-time adversary.

The new party strategy is to stress investment in areas within three time zones and having convenient transport links with Taiwan, which China has regarded as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949.

Okinawa, one of Japan's poorer prefectures, is as near to Taiwan as China and has direct air and sea links. Taiwan has banned direct transport, communications and other official links with China for nearly five decades.
Tokyo has diplomatic ties only with Beijing but has close economic and cultural ties with Taiwan.
